anomalies.observed: The +3V3 net includes both U20.2 (VO, power_out) and U21.13 (3V3OUT, power_out).
anomalies.expected: Only one power source should drive the +3V3 rail. When U21 is powered from +3V3, its 3V3OUT pin must be left unconnected.
anomalies.impact: Two 3.3V regulators driving the same rail can cause contention, excessive current, or damage to the FT231XS internal LDO.

anomalies.observed: The isolated CAN transceivers U10 and U11 have their logic-side ground (GND1) and bus-side ground (GND2) both connected to the common GND net. VCC2 is also connected to non-isolated 5V_switched_CAN.
anomalies.expected: For true galvanic isolation, GND1 and GND2 must be separate nets, and VCC2 must be supplied from an isolated DC-DC converter referenced to GND2.

evidence.quote: GND [High Power] : ... U10.4(GND1,power_in) U10.5(GND2,power_in) U11.4(GND1,power_in) U11.5(GND2,power_in) ...
two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion)

anomalies.impact: The isolation barrier is bypassed, so the CAN buses are not galvanically isolated. Ground loops and common-mode noise can couple between the CM4 and the motor controllers, potentially causing communication errors or damage.

anomalies.observed: The value field is SN74LVC1G07QDCKTQ1, but the MPN is U74LVC1G125G-AL5-R and the symbol has an active-low output enable (/OE) pin. The SN74LVC1G07 does not have an /OE pin; the SN74LVC1G125 does.
anomalies.expected: The value and library part should match the actual device. Since the circuit uses the /OE pin, the correct part is a 1G125 (or similar 3-state buffer), not a 1G07 open-drain buffer.
anomalies.impact: If assembled with the value (1G07), the /OE pin is not connected (NC on 1G07), so the enable control for e-stop sinks and LED power switching will not work. If assembled with the MPN (1G125), the board works as intended. The conflicting BOM data can lead to the wrong part being fitted.
